cluster_summary: This cluster includes 37 CVEs in XWiki where user-controlled input is embedded into template outputs (wiki syntax, HTML, URLs, scripts) without proper escaping or context-aware handling. The root causes vary: missing HTML escaping, missing wiki syntax escaping, missing URL encoding, missing validation, incomplete escaping functions, or improper use of rendering macros. All lead to injection of wiki macros, Velocity, Groovy, or HTML/JavaScript with server-side privileges.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-influenced inputs, resource identities, state values, or configuration described by the member CVEs into the sensitive operation or security boundary described by the member CVEs. Report code paths where the required validation, authorization, isolation, state check, or binding is absent or not connected to the sensitive effect. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 1 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should Override HTTP response Content-Type to 'text/plain' when the output syntax is not HTML or XHTML..

mechanism.missing_guard: the required validation, authorization, isolation, state check, or binding is absent or not connected to the sensitive effect
mechanism.name: Missing Content-Type enforcement for non-HTML output
mechanism.sink_shape: the sensitive operation or security boundary described by the member CVEs
mechanism.source_shape: attacker-influenced inputs, resource identities, state values, or configuration described by the member CVEs
mechanism.typical_fix: Override HTTP response Content-Type to 'text/plain' when the output syntax is not HTML or XHTML.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Override HTTP response Content-Type to 'text/plain' when the output syntax is not HTML or XHTML.
sub_patterns.name: Missing Content-Type enforcement for non-HTML output
sub_patterns.root_cause: Output syntax parameter changes the response body format but the Content-Type remains text/html, allowing user-supplied HTML to be rendered as active content.
